target_moa.text: Anthelmintic active against O. volvulus microfilariae; mechanism not fully known but thought to bind glutamate-gated chloride channels (GluCl), GABA receptors and/or ABC transporters, causing increased permeability, chloride influx, hyperpolarization and muscle paralysis.

citations.quote: Moxidectin is active against the microfilariae of *O. volvulus* [see Clinical Studies (14)].

Studies with other nematodes suggest that moxidectin binds to glutamate-gated chloride channels (GluCl), gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptors and/or ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. This leads to increased permeability, influx of chloride ions, hyperpolarization and muscle paralysis. Additionally,

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were eosinophilia (74% vs 79% ivermectin), pruritus (65% vs 54%), musculoskeletal pain (64% vs 52%), headache (58% vs 54%), and rash (37% vs 21%); most reflect Mazzotti reaction from microfilariae death. Serious/fatal encephalopathy may occur in Loa loa co-infected patients.

summary.text: Moxidectin received orphan drug designation for onchocerciasis (September 2010) and was reviewed as a Priority NDA; the sponsor was also granted a tropical disease priority review voucher under section 524 of the FDCA. Approval was based on the pivotal Phase 3 trial (Trial 1) demonstrating superiority over ivermectin in reducing skin microfilariae at 12 months, supported by a Phase 2 dose-ranging trial (Trial 2); it was a first-cycle, traditional approval (not accelerated).
